statement: Navarre and Aragon were united under Sancho III 'the Great' of Pamplona (1004–1035), who also controlled Castile and León temporarily — the closest medieval Iberia came to a single Christian kingdom before Ferdinand and Isabella. His death produced the familiar disaster: partition among sons. Aragon (under Ramiro I) and Navarre (under García III) became separate kingdoms that only reunited briefly under Alfonso I 'the Battler' (ruled both 1104–1134). Alfonso I's death without heirs permanently separated them: Aragon passed to Ramon Berenguer IV through marriage; Navarre elected García Ramírez.
